# Library shelf-label study: working notes

Fictional evaluation material. No real participants, sources, meetings, or study results are described here. Source L1 is supplied in full below.

## Researcher's direction

I want to test whether plain-language category labels help first-time visitors find a book. Keep the study about wording, with shelf locations, sign size, and layout unchanged. I have not chosen between successful retrieval within a time limit and completion time as the primary outcome. I want advice on a useful small first study, not a new app or a different research topic.

## Available evidence: L1, classroom exercise memo

In an earlier fictional class exercise, one group found 9 of 15 books under the old signage. A different group found 12 of 15 under revised signage. Both the wording and the sign locations changed.

## Current draft

Plain-language labels improve retrieval success by 20 percentage points and reduce librarians' workload. Our proposal will confirm this result with a small visitor study. We will print the labels, run sessions, and write up the outcome.

## Resources and dependencies

One researcher has six hours a week for three weeks and a printing budget of 30 USD. Access to the room and permission to run a visitor study are pending. A staff contact estimates that up to 12 volunteers might be available; nobody is recruited yet. Two 45-minute sessions have been suggested but are not booked. No advisor has given feedback. Relevant institutional requirements have not been checked.

## Tentative activity list

Week 1: read 20 papers and print the new labels. Week 2: complete two sessions. Week 3: make polished slides.
